summary.headline: Hindustan Foods Q2 FY27 adjusted PAT rose 22% YoY to INR46 crore despite a 1.5-month Silvassa flood disruption; FY27 PAT guidance above INR200 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR1,269 crore (+18% YoY), EBITDA INR115 crore (+26%), and adjusted PAT INR46 crore (+22%), with H1 adjusted PAT up about 30% to INR89 crore. Reported PAT was INR45 crore after INR1.3 crore of Silvassa flood-related exceptional losses. The footwear division returned to profitability in Q2 after a loss-making Q1, and H1 operating cash flow turned positive at over INR57 crore versus negative H2 FY26. Management guided to a strong H2, with about INR300 crore of projects commercialising from December and FY27 PAT above INR200 crore.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Returned to profitability in Q2 after a Q1 loss from raw material and wage cost increases on legacy fixed-price orders. October 2026 was the division's highest-ever monthly turnover, and the order book is full till March 2027.

segments.name: Home & personal care, food & beverages, ice cream, OTC pharma
segments.commentary: Management said these verticals saw healthy demand and capacity utilisation. OTC pharma has spare capacity at Baddi and Chennai, with audits and trials now yielding results.

segments.name: Silvassa facility
segments.commentary: Flooding caused about 1.5 months of disruption and a INR1.3 crore exceptional loss. Operations have since normalised, and the facility should reach ramped-up capacity by end-December 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of more than INR200 crore, with H2 requiring roughly 50% PAT growth per an analyst's reading of guidance.
About INR300 crore of capex commissioning from December 2026; benefit expected to show up mainly in Q4 FY27.

Project timelines revised after geopolitical and weather delays, which management said are not financially material. Malt beverages at Coimbatore and Ayurvedic supplements at Baddi are expected in Q4 FY27; a new CSD line at Guwahati in Q4 FY27; ice cream cone and sleeve line at Nashik in Q1 FY28.

Management expects significantly stronger operating cash flow in H2 FY27 from more customers moving to net revenue model from Q4 FY27 and easing of the inverted duty structure after recent GST changes.
Capital Markets Day planned for early December 2026, with FY28 plans to be detailed.
capex_capacity: Seasonal beverage and ice cream projects at Aurangabad, Mysuru, Hyderabad and Panipat are progressing and expected to be ready for the season.
Chennai shoe capacity expansion of nearly 20% in overall shoemaking capacity, with work already started for sports shoes.
Management targets a 60:40 dedicated-to-shared gross block split, but said this will fluctuate by quarter; dedicated factories target 16-22% ROCE and the blended target is around 18%.
Silvassa plant expected to run at ramped-up capacity by end of December 2026.
OTC pharma sites at Baddi and Chennai have spare capacity; management said throughput can nearly double before further capex.
demand_pricing: Management reported healthy volume growth across all verticals, with a broadening project pipeline.
Footwear: all fresh orders now secured at revised prices reflecting current cost structure; new brands onboarded for sports shoes and sneakers; order book exceeds capacity.
Management said it would be uncomfortable if any single customer exceeded 33% of any category's gross block or EBITDA; it stated this threshold has not been reached.
Pricing varies by product sophistication and automation rather than by category, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in shared-manufacturing EBITDA share and the dedicated gross block share (61% to 63%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA slide shows share, not margin; the shift came mainly from the footwear business turning profitable. Gross block is dynamic, so the 60:40 split should be viewed as a trend, not a quarterly figure.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company quantify the revenue and EBITDA impact of Silvassa, project delays and the net revenue transition together?
qa_highlights.answer: Mayank Samdani estimated INR3-4 crore of EBITDA that could have come in, which would have lifted quarterly PBT growth from about 24% to nearly 30%. Net revenue transition is EBITDA- and PAT-neutral.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 see weak growth given the emphasis on Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari declined to comment on Q3 numbers. He said only about one month of Q3 will include the new capacity, versus the full quarter in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 outlook for footwear beyond the March 2027 order visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not giving FY28 numbers, but is expanding Chennai capacity by about 20% because it expects structural growth and the margin recovery to reflect in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue has moved to the net revenue model and what is the optical revenue impact for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Newer customers have already moved, and one bigger customer is expected to switch from Q4 FY27. Management could not quantify the turnover impact, as the transition is not yet finalised.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company view food-safety inspections affecting juice and beverage customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said audits are routine for large factories. It expects regulatory scrutiny to push brands toward organised contract manufacturers, which it sees as a benefit.

risks_watch: Q4 FY27 carries most of the H2 earnings uplift; delays in commissioning from geopolitical or weather factors could push profit further out.
Working capital and inverted GST duty structure: cash flow recovery depends on more customers moving to net revenue model and on GST changes.
Footwear profitability is still recent and its FY28 outlook beyond March 2027 is not guided; prior quarters have shown losses.
OTC pharma utilisation is still ramping, and the segment has the longest gestation period.
Food-safety inspections in the beverages and juice segments are a sector-wide concern raised by an analyst.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the business and H2 recovery, but defensive about Q2 relative to expectations; management acknowledged the Silvassa delay cost roughly INR3-4 crore of EBITDA. It was evasive on Q3 growth, the FY28 footwear outlook, and the quantum of the net revenue model shift.
key_quotes: Our footwear division, which had gone through a challenging Q1 due to the raw material costs and wage pressures, returned to profitability in Q2.
Q2 should have been the record quarter.
Importantly, this transition does not change our absolute profitability.
